ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 16th January 2016,
passed by the Court of Senior Civil Judge, JMFC and MACT, Nanjangud, (for short `Tribunal'), in MVC No.35/2014, seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: NC: 2025:KHC:25141 HC-KAR
Though this appeal is slated for admission, with the consent of both the sides, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, on 06.05.2013, petitioner met with an accident at Madahalli, due to rash and negligent driving of the bus belonging to respondent- corporation bearing registration No.KA-09-F-4025 by its driver.
As a result, the claimant sustained fracture of right 2nd rib, fracture of lower end of right-radius, fracture of styloid process of right ulna and other minor injuries.
He took treatment as inpatient for a week and spent substantial amount towards medical expenses.
He was an agriculturist, earning Rs. 8,000/- per month through cultivation of his own land and other lands.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident, he has suffered permanent disability.
With these reasons, he prayed to award compensation of Rs.2,55,000/-.

sentences.text: The respondent-Corporation filed a written statement denying the contents of the claim petition.
It further contended that the claimant was a pedestrian and that the incident occurred due to his own negligence, and not because he was traveling in the vehicle.
The Corporation also denied the claimant's entitlement to compensation and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
6. This claim petition was clubbed with MVC No.34/2014 and common evidence was recorded in both the cases.
The claimants in both the cases together examined 4 witnesses as PW-1 to PW-4 and marked 38 documents, as per Exs.P-1 to P-38.
Respondents have not led any oral and documentary evidence.
NC: 2025:KHC:25141 HC-KAR 7.

The Tribunal after hearing both the parties, by the impugned judgment and award, awarded the following amount of compensation:
 Particulars Amount in Rs.
Pain and sufferings 60,000/-

Medical expenses (including diet, 5,000/-
nourishment, attendant charges etc.,) Loss of earnings due to disability 47,520/-
 Loss of amenities 10,000/-
 Total 1,22,520/-
 Rounded off 1,23,000/-
8.

The Tribunal has assessed the age of the claimant as 52 years, his earnings as Rs.6,000/- p.m.,
disability at 7% to the whole body, applied the multiplier as '11' and on that basis, calculated the compensation.
The claimant found the compensation is inadequate and has filed this appeal, to seek enhancement.

Fact of accident is undisputed and hence, need to relook into the said findings.
NC: 2025:KHC:25141 HC-KAR 9.
I have heard the arguments and anxiously perused the records.

Considering the contentions of the claimant as well as documents placed on record and evidence of the doctor who issued the disability certificate, the amount of compensation awarded under some of the heads appears to be on the K S Shivanna vs Fakeergowda on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50252052/
3 lower side.
10.
The claimant contended that he was earning Rs.8,000/- p.m. and it was not excessive or exorbitant.
If we follow the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the income of the claimant can be accepted as Rs.8,000/- p.m. instead of Rs.6,000/- p.m. as assessed by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid up period' and has not awarded adequate compensation towards 'special diet, attendant charges and conveyance charges'.
The disability stated by PW-4 is 18% to 20% and he has also assessed disability of 4% to 5% due to fracture of ribs.

The disability assessed by PW-4 is physical disability;
when it is converted to the whole body's NC: 2025:KHC:25141 HC-KAR functional disability, it will be 1/3rd of the upper limb.
Considering the same, the Tribunal has assessed disability as 7%.
It does not call for any interference.

On re-appreciating the materials available on record, claimant is entitled to following amount of compensation:
 Particulars Amount in Rs.
 Pain and sufferings 75,000/-
 Medical expenses 2,000/-
 Special diet, conveyance and 20,000/-
 attendant charges  Loss of income during laid up period 24,000/-
 (Rs.8,000/- x 3)
 Loss of future earning capacity due to 73,920/-
 disability  (Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 11 x 7%)
 Loss of amenities and future 25,000/-
 unhappiness  Total 2,19,920/-
 Amount awarded by the Tribunal 1,23,000/-
 Enhancement- 96,920/-
 Rounded off- 97,000/-

4 11.
The claimant is entitled to interest on the said amount, at the rate of 6% per annum.
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the same.

12. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 16th January 2016, passed in MVC.No.35/2014, by the Senior Civil Judge, JMFC and MACT, Nanjangud, stands modified.

iii) The claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.97,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
iv) The enhancement is marginal.
Therefore, entire amount is ordered to be released in favour of claimant on due identification.
v) Draw award accordingly.

HC-KAR Registry is directed to send back the records along with a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal.
